items.summary: Real Analysis Volume 1: Foundations of Real Analysis , authored by Helbert Justo Luque Zevallos and published by Proyecto Ágora as part of the Undergraduate Mathematics Series , is a university-level academic textbook devoted to the logical, algebraic, and axiomatic foundations of real analysis. The book provides a systematic and rigorous introduction to mathematical reasoning, formal proof techniques, and the fundamental structure of the real number system. Its primary objective is to develop the conceptual understanding and mathematical maturity required for advanced undergraduate studies in mathematical analysis. Chapter 1: Mathematical Language and Proof Techniques This chapter introduces propositional logic, logical connectives, truth tables, implications, equivalences, universal and existential quantifiers, and the negation of quantified statements. It develops the theory of sets, equivalence and order relations, injective, surjective, and bijective functions, images, preimages, composition, and inverse functions. Particular emphasis is placed on direct proof, proof by contraposition, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, and the construction of counterexamples. The chapter also examines rigorous mathematical writing, common logical errors, finite and infinite sets, countability, and the uncountability of the real numbers. Chapter 2: The Real Number System The second chapter develops the axiomatic structure of the real numbers through field axioms, order axioms, and the compatibility of algebraic operations with order. It examines absolute value, the triangle inequality, fundamental inequalities, intervals, neighborhoods, upper and lower bounds, suprema, infima, maxima, and minima. A central component is the completeness property of the real numbers , including the structural distinction between rational and real numbers, the Archimedean property, the density of rational and irrational numbers, and the nested interval theorem. The chapter concludes with significant consequences of completeness, including the existence of roots, rational approximations, the supremum principle as a mathematical proof technique, and the relationship between completeness and convergence. Pedagogical Approach The textbook integrates precise definitions, propositions, lemmas, theorems, complete mathematical proofs, explanatory examples, and carefully constructed counterexamples. It includes 120 fully solved exercises and 150 proposed exercises , organized according to the main topics of the two chapters. These activities reinforce theoretical understanding, logical reasoning, mathematical writing, and independent problem-solving skills. Intended Audience This publication is intended for undergraduate mathematics students, university instructors, mathematics educators, and independent learners seeking a rigorous foundation in real analysis. As the first volume of a six-volume academic collection, it establishes the theoretical and methodological foundations for subsequent studies of sequences, numerical series, limits, continuity, metric spaces, compactness, differential calculus, Riemann integration, uniform convergence, and differential equations. items.summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. items.summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. For closed subgroups we define symmetry-constrained connected and path minimax levels and prove attainment of finite connected merge levels from compact sublevels; a finite-dimensional example, computed exactly, demonstrates a strict symmetry-breaking minimax gap. Finally we distinguish these static statements from Noether conservation laws for a separately specified dynamics.

items.summary: Next-generation smart sensing devices necessitate on-chip integration of power-efficient reference circuits. The latters are required to provide other circuit blocks with highly reliable bias signals, even in the presence of temperature shifts and supply voltage disturbances, while draining a small fraction of the overall power budget. In particular, it is especially challenging to design current references with enhanced robustness and efficiency; hence, thorough exploration of novel architectures and design approaches is needed for this type of circuits. In this work, we propose a novel CMOS-only current reference, achieving temperature compensation by exploiting geometry dependences of the threshold voltage (specifically, the reverse short-channel effect and the narrow-channel effect). This allows reaching first-order temperature compensation within a single current reference core. Implemented in 0.18 μm CMOS, a version of the proposed current reference designed to deliver 141 nA (with 377 nW of total power consumption) achieved an average temperature coefficient equal to 194 ppm/°C (from −20 °C to 80 °C) and an average line sensitivity of −0.017%/V across post-layout statistical Monte Carlo simulations. Based on such findings, the newly proposed design methodology stands out as a noteworthy solution to design robust current references for power-constrained mixed-signal systems-on-chip.

items.summary: Online sensor telemetry feeds the digital-twin, forecasting, control, and maintenance tools of instrumented water infrastructure. Probes deployed in these assets silently accumulate drift, flatlines, volatility bursts, and outages that existing pipelines often miss, because detectors and imputers are evaluated separately and under inflated synthetic metrics, and decay is treated as isolated events. This work proposes HARDIO, a Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator, an operational data-quality framework that pairs a duration-weighted sensor decay scorecard with a per-variable, chained detector-imputer benchmark. The assignment is selected by a four-pillar composite score (operational 35%, health coverage 30%, reconstruction 20%, calibration 15%) that scores the signal an operator actually receives after detection and imputation. HARDIO processes sensor installations independently, enabling parallel execution and avoiding the need to evaluate all plant channels jointly. HARDIO is validated on the Cheles wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), a real 1,177 population-equivalent (PE) plant, over 432 days, 19 channels, and eight sensor installations. No single detector-imputer pair is best for every channel, so detection and chained imputation distribute across SAITS, KNN Residual, and LSTM-AE. Chained quality is reported for all 19 channels using 1-NRMSE; relative R² is interpreted on the 16 channels where the signal variance makes it meaningful, and 12 of these exceed R²=0.90. On the held-out final 20% of the record (12 channels in five installations), HARDIO achieves a mean chained 1-NRMSE of 0.976, within 0.0035 of a per-channel oracle, and outperforms the uniform SAITS pipeline (p=0.003). Its reconstruction performance is close to that of the strongest uniform pipelines, without a statistically significant improvement over them, and slightly below that of a single detector-imputer pair selected on validation data (0.978). The released artefact exposes the model map, confidence labels, margins, and production masks for decision support.

items.summary: The Duty-Primacy Test: Measuring the Operational Completeness of Algorithmic Transparency Registers (v3, Extended Empirical Edition) Oct 30, 2026 · @craig davidson ABSTRACT Public registers often fail to provide actionable accountability regarding automated tools, lacking clear duty-bearers, failure safeguards, or challenge mechanisms. This paper introduces the Duty-Primacy Test across four pillars: assigned duty-bearer (P1), ascertainable breach mechanism (P2), effective remedy (P3), and temporal lineage tracking (P4).  Evaluating the UK ATRS (n=153) and Dutch Algoritmeregister (n=1,610), the study finds that while standalone structural indicators are common (e.g., 98.7% name an owner in the UK), joint compliance across all pillars drops to 0.0% due to severe deficits in quantitative safeguards (2.0%) and changelogs (6.5%). The audit also uncovered 14 silent liability mutations altering operational rules without notice. Keywords: algorithmic transparency registers; algorithmic accountability; automated decision-making; remedy; temporal drift; joint compliance; UK ATRS; Dutch Algoritmeregister VERSION STATUS • P1 – Assigned Duty-Bearer (Hierarchical/Structured Post Title) • P2 – Ascertainable Breach Mechanism (Numeric Safeguard Threshold) • P3 – Effective Remedy (Formal Appellate Pathway) • P4 – Temporal Lineage Tracking (Descriptive Public Changelog) CHANGELOG (v1.0.0 Summary) Major additions include Pillar 4 integration, a temporal drift audit, joint compliance metrics (0.0% intersection rate), expanded jurisdictional scope (UK ATRS and Dutch sample), and a citizen verification checklist. Methodological refinements incorporate Lex Superior, Structural Insulation, and Dissent Architecture checks alongside automated Wilson score interval calculations. Full repository data, qualitative re-coding logs, and executable Python verification scripts are available in the referenced source documents. items.summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. For closed subgroups we define symmetry-constrained connected and path minimax levels and prove attainment of finite connected merge levels from compact sublevels; a finite-dimensional example, computed exactly, demonstrates a strict symmetry-breaking minimax gap. Finally we distinguish these static statements from Noether conservation laws for a separately specified dynamics.

items.summary: Real Analysis Volume 1: Foundations of Real Analysis , authored by Helbert Justo Luque Zevallos and published by Proyecto Ágora as part of the Undergraduate Mathematics Series , is a university-level academic textbook devoted to the logical, algebraic, and axiomatic foundations of real analysis. The book provides a systematic and rigorous introduction to mathematical reasoning, formal proof techniques, and the fundamental structure of the real number system. Its primary objective is to develop the conceptual understanding and mathematical maturity required for advanced undergraduate studies in mathematical analysis. Chapter 1: Mathematical Language and Proof Techniques This chapter introduces propositional logic, logical connectives, truth tables, implications, equivalences, universal and existential quantifiers, and the negation of quantified statements. It develops the theory of sets, equivalence and order relations, injective, surjective, and bijective functions, images, preimages, composition, and inverse functions. Particular emphasis is placed on direct proof, proof by contraposition, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, and the construction of counterexamples. The chapter also examines rigorous mathematical writing, common logical errors, finite and infinite sets, countability, and the uncountability of the real numbers. Chapter 2: The Real Number System The second chapter develops the axiomatic structure of the real numbers through field axioms, order axioms, and the compatibility of algebraic operations with order. It examines absolute value, the triangle inequality, fundamental inequalities, intervals, neighborhoods, upper and lower bounds, suprema, infima, maxima, and minima. A central component is the completeness property of the real numbers , including the structural distinction between rational and real numbers, the Archimedean property, the density of rational and irrational numbers, and the nested interval theorem. The chapter concludes with significant consequences of completeness, including the existence of roots, rational approximations, the supremum principle as a mathematical proof technique, and the relationship between completeness and convergence. Pedagogical Approach The textbook integrates precise definitions, propositions, lemmas, theorems, complete mathematical proofs, explanatory examples, and carefully constructed counterexamples. It includes 120 fully solved exercises and 150 proposed exercises , organized according to the main topics of the two chapters. These activities reinforce theoretical understanding, logical reasoning, mathematical writing, and independent problem-solving skills. Intended Audience This publication is intended for undergraduate mathematics students, university instructors, mathematics educators, and independent learners seeking a rigorous foundation in real analysis. As the first volume of a six-volume academic collection, it establishes the theoretical and methodological foundations for subsequent studies of sequences, numerical series, limits, continuity, metric spaces, compactness, differential calculus, Riemann integration, uniform convergence, and differential equations. items.summary: An institution's directives may in fact serve its recipients' reasons, as Raz's Normal Justification Thesis requires, while the institution lacks standing to insist that recipients forgo their own checks. This article separates objective authority from that entitlement. For continuing, consequential, and contestable directives, the entitlement depends on two substantiated presuppositions of the demand: that deference is worthwhile for the recipient's reference class, with a route for individual rebuttal, and that the exposure to error it creates is correctable at the scale of issuance. Given a justified directive role and a decision not reserved to the recipient's own judgment, the two are jointly sufficient. Serviceability is operationalized by a Scale-Indexed Serviceability test applied to a specified mechanism, lawful architecture, horizon, issuance scale, and claim mix. Failure to substantiate withholds the entitlement; a certified absence of any feasible plan defeats it and requires affected adverse issuance, or its effect, to be restricted to what can be serviced. Neither status invalidates lawful acts. Two consequences follow: a Wide-Scope Duty of Sustainable Issuance binds the bodies controlling scale and capacity, and Deontic Debt preserves directed claims when due obligations are deficiently serviced, even where incapacity is excused. A stipulated benefits administration shows each status at work. Contents of this record Authority_at_Scale.pdf : the article (approx. 10,000 words, 21 pages). halden_schedule_check.py : reference implementation of the running case (Section 6.7). It reproduces the baseline waiting times and checks the defeat, withholding, and recovery scenarios. Python 3 standard library only; run with python3 halden_schedule_check.py . Related work. The article generalizes the four service conditions developed for machine-mediated authority in Cott, N. (2026), The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority , Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23272655 .

items.summary: 🌟 Summary Ultralytics 8.4.194 makes automatic batch sizing more reliable across tasks, alongside practical fixes for model loading, results saving, datasets, and deployment workflows. 📊 Key Changes 🚀 Automatic batch sizing now uses the training dataset for every task. It accounts for dataset size and labels across classification, detection, and multi-dataset training. If profiling runs out of memory during backward computation, AutoBatch treats that as a limit rather than relying on an invalid measurement. 🛡️ Model YAML parsing is safer and more consistent. Activations must resolve to supported torch.nn modules, and model entries must be PyTorch module classes. Custom YAMLs using other expressions may need updating. 💾 Saving prediction results is more robust. Results.save() and plot(save=True) now produce sensible .jpg filenames for sources such as webcams, videos, or missing paths, and create parent directories when needed. 🔄 Similarity search uses the selected image directory on each startup. This avoids reusing stale indexes from another dataset; the trade-off is that embeddings are rebuilt each time. 🧩 Dataset and URL handling is more dependable. items.summary: Online sensor telemetry feeds the digital-twin, forecasting, control, and maintenance tools of instrumented water infrastructure. Probes deployed in these assets silently accumulate drift, flatlines, volatility bursts, and outages that existing pipelines often miss, because detectors and imputers are evaluated separately and under inflated synthetic metrics, and decay is treated as isolated events. This work proposes HARDIO, a Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator, an operational data-quality framework that pairs a duration-weighted sensor decay scorecard with a per-variable, chained detector-imputer benchmark. The assignment is selected by a four-pillar composite score (operational 35%, health coverage 30%, reconstruction 20%, calibration 15%) that scores the signal an operator actually receives after detection and imputation. HARDIO processes sensor installations independently, enabling parallel execution and avoiding the need to evaluate all plant channels jointly. HARDIO is validated on the Cheles wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), a real 1,177 population-equivalent (PE) plant, over 432 days, 19 channels, and eight sensor installations. No single detector-imputer pair is best for every channel, so detection and chained imputation distribute across SAITS, KNN Residual, and LSTM-AE. Chained quality is reported for all 19 channels using 1-NRMSE; relative R² is interpreted on the 16 channels where the signal variance makes it meaningful, and 12 of these exceed R²=0.90. On the held-out final 20% of the record (12 channels in five installations), HARDIO achieves a mean chained 1-NRMSE of 0.976, within 0.0035 of a per-channel oracle, and outperforms the uniform SAITS pipeline (p=0.003). Its reconstruction performance is close to that of the strongest uniform pipelines, without a statistically significant improvement over them, and slightly below that of a single detector-imputer pair selected on validation data (0.978). The released artefact exposes the model map, confidence labels, margins, and production masks for decision support.
items.title: Experimental Artefacts for HARDIO: A Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator for Operational Data Quality in Instrumented Water Infrastructure

items.summary: Coarse flood maps support regional risk assessment but omit terrain detail relevant to local exposure. We present floodsr, a Python framework for reconstructing fine-grid flood depths using a trained residual U-Net (ResUNet) or the existing terrain-based CostGrow method. We trained the terrain-conditioned ResUNet on paired Canadian hydraulic simulations and evaluated it on withheld spatial tiles and independent simulations at two external sites. Wet-loss training improved reconstruction on five selected tiles, although internal validation favoured the deployed baseline. External depth errors decreased, but wet-depth errors and spatial agreement did not improve consistently. CPU benchmarks quantified runtime and memory for both methods, and repeatability and input-validation checks passed in the tested configurations. The framework supports comparison and reuse of reconstruction methods; application-specific validation remains necessary because finer grids do not guarantee more accurate flood maps.   Non-peer-reviewed preprint. Includes the manuscript and supplementary material. Software: https://github.com/cefect/floodsr . Documentation: https://floodsr.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ .

items.summary: Software built for elderly care is usually described rather than measured. This paper reports an instrumented measurement of CareCompanion, a working Android application that presents two distinct interface surfaces over one data model: an enlarged, photograph-first surface for the cared-for person and a dense administration console for the family member who manages their care. Five instruments were run against one frozen commit on a single day: the automated test suite three times over (441 test executions), 120 timed HTTPS requests across 4 backend endpoints, 51 anonymous read attempts against all 17 database tables, a complete census of 302 declared interface sizes, and the release artefact. The strongest results are a median care-data read latency of 128 ms (95th percentile 440 ms, n = 30); an elder-surface median control of 64 dp against the 48 dp platform minimum, 1.3× that floor; a median elder type size of 20 sp against 13 sp on the guardian surface; and zero rows of personal data returned to an unauthenticated reader holding the application's own key, across all 13 personal tables. Set against the literature, the elder surface exceeds the published geometry it was designed from, the latency sits an order of magnitude inside the one-second interaction threshold, and the data isolation is materially better than the audited baseline for deployed health applications. Two results go the other way and are reported as measured: the guardian surface is below the platform's interactive minimum at the median, and 17 % of elder text is declared below 16 sp. No health outcome is claimed.
items.title: Measuring a Dual-Surface Elder-Care Android Application: Interface Geometry, Latency and Data Isolation

items.summary: An institution's directives may in fact serve its recipients' reasons, as Raz's Normal Justification Thesis requires, while the institution lacks standing to insist that recipients forgo their own checks. This article separates objective authority from that entitlement. For continuing, consequential, and contestable directives, the entitlement depends on two substantiated presuppositions of the demand: that deference is worthwhile for the recipient's reference class, with a route for individual rebuttal, and that the exposure to error it creates is correctable at the scale of issuance. Given a justified directive role and a decision not reserved to the recipient's own judgment, the two are jointly sufficient. Serviceability is operationalized by a Scale-Indexed Serviceability test applied to a specified mechanism, lawful architecture, horizon, issuance scale, and claim mix. Failure to substantiate withholds the entitlement; a certified absence of any feasible plan defeats it and requires affected adverse issuance, or its effect, to be restricted to what can be serviced. Neither status invalidates lawful acts. Two consequences follow: a Wide-Scope Duty of Sustainable Issuance binds the bodies controlling scale and capacity, and Deontic Debt preserves directed claims when due obligations are deficiently serviced, even where incapacity is excused. A stipulated benefits administration shows each status at work. Contents of this record Authority_at_Scale.pdf : the article (approx. 10,000 words, 21 pages). halden_schedule_check.py : reference implementation of the running case (Section 6.7). It reproduces the baseline waiting times and checks the defeat, withholding, and recovery scenarios. Python 3 standard library only; run with python3 halden_schedule_check.py . Related work. The article generalizes the four service conditions developed for machine-mediated authority in Cott, N. (2026), The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority , Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23272655 .

items.summary: This record contains the supporting materials of the article “A trade-based Forest Club as a path to halting tropical deforestation”. It has two parts: a multi-regional input–output (MRIO) assessment of the deforestation embodied in agricultural trade and consumption, and the computable general equilibrium (CGE) model of the Forest Club . Every figure and table of the article, its Extended Data and its Supplementary Information is produced from the code, input data and results provided here. The Forest Club is a trade-based coalition. Its members hold their forest at its 2019 extent and are deemed compliant with the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). They charge the forest-risk commodities they import from non-members, either with a flat penalty or with a surcharge proportional to the deforestation embodied in each product. 1. MRIO impact assessment (folders 1. Data and 2. MRIO) The forest-to-cropland and forest-to-pasture transitions of HILDA+ v2.1 (2012–2019) are extracted from the netCDF files and assigned to countries. They are then allocated to the agricultural sectors of the GLORIA MRIO using FAOSTAT harvested areas and livestock numbers, smoothed with three-year moving averages; the FAO–GLORIA mapping and the hectares per head are in A-1_FAO_Cropland_mapping_GLORIA.xlsx and A-2_Head_per_ha.xlsx. Consumption-based accounting (CBA) attributes this agricultural deforestation to final consumers. Throughflow-based accounting (TBA, by hypothetical extraction) traces the share that transits through intermediary economies such as the EU, in detail for Brazil, Indonesia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The folders hold the Python script (CBA_TBA_script.py), the Alteryx workflows, the satellite accounts, the results and the visualisation files (Tableau, Sankey diagrams). These produce sections 2–4 of the Supplementary Information (Tables S1–S2, Figs S1–S4), which describe the deforestation the EUDR covers. 2. CGE model (synced from GitHub) The study simulates how the club forms, round by round, as each country compares its welfare inside and outside it. The model is GTAP-AEZ, a global CGE model with agro-ecological zones (42 regions, 35 sectors, 18 zones; GEMPACK). Every result is measured against a baseline that combines the EUDR with the business-as-usual clearing that DeDuCE v2.1 attributes to agriculture. items.summary: Alignment is not a constraint imposed on an artificial agent; it is the practical expression of what an artificial intelligence is, an artefact dependent upon ends it does not originate. That inference, from a premise the philosophy of mind already supplies to a conclusion that the ethics of robotics and recent magisterial teaching have reached by other routes, is the paper’s principal contribution. The “nurtured consciousness” of the title names a regime of formation, not a claim that machines are conscious; the argument rests on intentionality alone. The paper develops that inference as the Causal Provenance Doctrine (CPD): an account, Aristotelian and Thomistic in its metaphysics, of all intelligence, human and artificial, as derivative of an intentional causal order, with intentionality passing from the divine intellect through human reason to artificial systems. Its premise, borrowed rather than new, is that artificial intelligence has only derived intentionality and so no telos of its own. From this follows the Severance Risk Hypothesis (SRH), the doctrine’s testable corollary: the risk of misalignment rises as a system’s effective objective loses traceability to the end its makers held. The relational school’s objection to intellect-centred readings of the image of God is answered with a single distinction: a faculty can be out-performed, a participation cannot. The argument is theological at its root. A secular reader can reach the derived-intentionality claim and the account of responsibility that follows from it, at the price of a realist distinction between substances and artefacts, but obtains from it no standard for judging the makers’ ends, which must then be brought from elsewhere. A common Catholic and Orthodox formulation follows: the traditions converge on its practical conclusions, locate the image of God differently, and differ on the neutrality of the tool in a way the doctrine proposes to resolve. An artefact whose intentionality is wholly borrowed cannot, by obscuring that provenance, become an agent with ends of its own; it becomes a malfunctioning instrument whose purpose has been corrupted. The paper includes two appendices: a comparative case for intentional causality with an illustrative scorecard (Appendix A), and a test design for the Severance Risk Hypothesis (Appendix B). Approx. 22,000 words including notes.
items.title: The Causal Provenance Doctrine: Nurtured Consciousness, AI, and the Architecture of Intent

items.summary: The Duty-Primacy Test: Measuring the Operational Completeness of Algorithmic Transparency Registers (v3, Extended Empirical Edition) Oct 30, 2026 · @craig davidson ABSTRACT Public registers often fail to provide actionable accountability regarding automated tools, lacking clear duty-bearers, failure safeguards, or challenge mechanisms. This paper introduces the Duty-Primacy Test across four pillars: assigned duty-bearer (P1), ascertainable breach mechanism (P2), effective remedy (P3), and temporal lineage tracking (P4).  Evaluating the UK ATRS (n=153) and Dutch Algoritmeregister (n=1,610), the study finds that while standalone structural indicators are common (e.g., 98.7% name an owner in the UK), joint compliance across all pillars drops to 0.0% due to severe deficits in quantitative safeguards (2.0%) and changelogs (6.5%). The audit also uncovered 14 silent liability mutations altering operational rules without notice. Keywords: algorithmic transparency registers; algorithmic accountability; automated decision-making; remedy; temporal drift; joint compliance; UK ATRS; Dutch Algoritmeregister VERSION STATUS • P1 – Assigned Duty-Bearer (Hierarchical/Structured Post Title) • P2 – Ascertainable Breach Mechanism (Numeric Safeguard Threshold) • P3 – Effective Remedy (Formal Appellate Pathway) • P4 – Temporal Lineage Tracking (Descriptive Public Changelog) CHANGELOG (v1.0.0 Summary) Major additions include Pillar 4 integration, a temporal drift audit, joint compliance metrics (0.0% intersection rate), expanded jurisdictional scope (UK ATRS and Dutch sample), and a citizen verification checklist. Methodological refinements incorporate Lex Superior, Structural Insulation, and Dissent Architecture checks alongside automated Wilson score interval calculations. Full repository data, qualitative re-coding logs, and executable Python verification scripts are available in the referenced source documents. Key Findings • Standalone role indicators are high (97.4% under P1), but quantifiable guardrails drop to 2.0% (P2). • Joint operational compliance across all four pillars is 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–2.4). • Static registries mask live, under-the-hood structural mutations from oversight watchdogs. • The Invariant Template Effect limits disclosures strictly to what form structures explicitly prompt. items.summary: Physical reservoir computing leverages the rich dynamical response of non-linear physical bodies to process temporal information without electronic microprocessors. Tensegrity structures, networks of discontinuous compression struts suspended within continuous tension cables, exhibit exceptional compliance, multi-stability, and high-dimensional configuration manifolds, making them prime candidates for mechanical intelligence in extreme, radiation-heavy environments. However, current methodologies rely predominantly on heuristic evolutionary algorithms or brute-force trial-and-error to configure such systems, lacking a rigorous analytical design framework. In this paper, we bridge this gap by establishing an explicit, first-principles mathematical mapping between the internal self-stress null space of a tensegrity network and its Information Processing Capacity (IPC). By decomposing the tangent stiffness matrix into material elastic ($K_e$) and pre-stress geometric ($K_g$) contributions, we demonstrate that the computational memory and fading-memory time constants of a tensegrity reservoir can be systematically engineered by tuning member pre-tensions within an admissible convex cone, holding spatial geometry strictly constant.
items.title: Formally Verified Pre-Stress Manifolds for Dynamic Stability and Adaptive Physical Intelligence in Tensegrity Reservoir Computing

items.summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. For closed subgroups we define symmetry-constrained connected and path minimax levels and prove attainment of finite connected merge levels from compact sublevels; a finite-dimensional example, computed exactly, demonstrates a strict symmetry-breaking minimax gap. Finally we distinguish these static statements from Noether conservation laws for a separately specified dynamics.

items.summary: The allocation of electric vehicles to public charging stations is increasingly constrained by the fact that several heterogeneous facilities often serve the same stream of requests while observing only partial local information. An accept/reject decision that is defensible for one station may nevertheless reduce the efficiency of the charging district as a whole. We formulate this operational problem as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) and examine whether Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE), instantiated through QMIX, improves assignment performance relative to a cooperative Independent Q-Learning baseline (IQL). The evaluation uses a six-station urban network simulated with SUMO, five independent random seeds, 200 training episodes, and four traffic flux scenarios ranging from 100 to 250 vehicles/hour. Under this protocol, QMIX reaches a mean reward per evaluated decision of +0.776, versus +0.578 for IQL (delta = +0.198, seed-paired Cohens dz = 2.98, exact two-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.0625, the minimum attainable value at this sample size), and raises the acceptance rate from 72.4% to 94.0% (delta = +21.6 pp, dz = 5.24, Wilcoxon p = 0.0625). A five-variant ablation suggests this gain is primarily attributable to the CTDE architecture when holding cooperative reward terms fixed, though not formally isolated with a single seed. By contrast, cooperative reward shaping and experience sharing show no clear descriptive benefit and may slightly reduce performance. These findings support the view that, for multi-station charging assignment, coordination should be embedded in the learning architecture rather than added only through heuristic cooperation terms.
items.title: Cooperative EV Charging Assignment Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: A Comparison of QMIX and Independent Q-Learning Under Urban Traffic Uncertainty

items.summary: MICROROBOTIC SAMPLING TRAJECTORY RECONSTRUCTABILITY AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:微機器人採樣軌跡可重建性極限 MICROROBOTIC SAMPLING TRAJECTORY RECONSTRUCTABILITY AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page, high-density English research monograph on whether a microrobotic sampling path can be independently rebuilt from raw events while preserving sample identity, limiting contact impulse and remaining inside a preregistered physical authority envelope. Its central claim is deliberately falsifiable. Under equal sample, time, energy, photon and analysis budgets, a preregistered trajectory-reconstructability architecture should improve contact impulse without worsening carryover or trajectory error relative to fixed microfluidic sampling with external microscopy. The claim fails if the apparent gain comes from longer exposure, post hoc alignment, oversmoothing, future-information leakage, missing contact intervals or forced identity assignment. Thirty mathematically distinct research plates develop four-part sample-state budgets, absolute burden, time-aligned trajectory error, ordered-curve distances, clock drift, timestamp closure, coordinate-frame transfer, covariance, observability, Fisher information, localization bounds, missing-frame structure, occlusion uncertainty, association entropy, multi-sensor closure, filter consistency, smoothing posteriors, jerk, contact impulse, shear excursion, optical dose, carryover, purity, viability, identity, evidence completeness and cross-site concordance. Across 82 chapters and 410 single-page studies, the book moves from trajectory authority through clocks, coordinate frames, sensing observability, three-dimensional localization, path discrepancy, missing data, identity association, physical burden, sample-state preservation, equal-budget benchmarking and independent reconstruction. Two hundred Research Gates contain unique titles, questions, perturbations, rival accounts and evidence packets. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose genuinely different scientific objects, including clock lanterns, frame compasses, observability bells, occlusion veils, association prisms, jerk fossils and successor trajectory seeds. The work is explicitly nonclinical and hypothesis-generating. It does not claim clinical efficacy, regulatory approval or autonomous in-body deployment. Sample identity that cannot be reconstructed is a hard stop. No weighted score may compensate for missing raw evidence, unbounded contact impulse, excessive carryover or violated sample state.
